name: maybe_Os_SetRuntimeFlag
summary: Takes the global runtime lock and sets the one-byte runtime-ready flag at 0x007AE4A1; looks like a one-shot init or finalisation hook.
evidence: No callers and no data pointer to the address, so it is not reached by the game's normal call graph. Body: bl 0x111D50 then strb #1 to [0x007AE4A0+1]. 0x111D50 is the -1/-2 lock-state helper around the arbitrate syscall, so this is lock plus flag bookkeeping, not game logic.

name: Save_InitPartySnapshot
summary: Clears and defaults the 0xc8b0-byte party snapshot used by save/load: 31 actor state blocks of 0x200 at +0x1830, 54 20-byte records at +0x5630, inventory arrays and checksum fields at +0xe0d8..+0xe0f0.
evidence: All four callers (0x2CCC00, 0x2CD2A0, 0x2CD498, 0x2CE5B4) construct the same object; 0x2CE5B4 accepts exactly arg4==0xc8b0 and verifies func_0051BB08(data,...,-1) against a stored checksum before copying the blob into +0x1830. 0x2CD2A0 copies 31*0x200 bytes from func_0035EB98(world,i)+0xc8 (the actor equipment/status block). Defaults 0x2ae, 0xffff, 0x104c, 0x3ae0 come from g_0010F640..g_0010F650.

name: maybe_Save_CompleteAsyncRead
summary: Finishes an asynchronous save/load request by passing the request fields at +0x14..+0x24 to the read worker and then storing state 5 in the shared work object at 0x007B00E0.
evidence: Calls func_001170CC(self->f_14, self->f_18, self->f_1c, self->f_20, self->f_24); 0x1170CC is the SVC-0x28/save-read worker and also writes *g_00117990 (0x007B00E0). Here the same address is written with 5, so this is the completion callback for that worker.

name: maybe_Save_BeginLoad
summary: Resets the load state of the save object (state 2, clears +0xe120 for 0x2a0 bytes) and initialises the lock word at +0xe118 before a read starts.
evidence: Sibling of Save_InitPartySnapshot: sets f_e3c4/f_e3c0/f_e3c5=0, f_e110=2 and calls the same lock helper func_0011CC10 on &self->f_e118. Called from the five 0x248xxx / 0x25Dxxx paths that start a load, and the -1/-2 state handling matches func_00111D50.

name: maybe_Os_MutexLock
summary: Blocking lock acquire on a two-state lock word: -1 becomes 0 and -2 becomes 1, each transition guarded by hasExclusiveAccess and the arbitrate syscall.
evidence: 31 callers including the CRT init path 0x00106440, the save worker 0x001170CC and the 0x2CCC00 constructors. The hasExclusiveAccess/ldrex loop plus func_0011CC10(*g_00111E04, arg1, 0, 1, 0, 0) is the standard 3DS kernel mutex arbitrate pattern; the exact public nn::os API name is not recoverable from the binary.

name: maybe_Save_BuildSectionList
summary: Walks a 0x274c-byte table of function-pointer slots, invokes each handler and chains the results into a tagged list with a running id; part of the save-snapshot construction, but the handlers themselves were not recoverable.
evidence: Iterates self+0x34..self+0x2780 (0x274c bytes, 4-byte slots) dispatching through the table at g_00115928 (0x0072D76C) with an index from f_10. Stores the result tag in f_16c/f_170 and the id in f_174, then calls func_0011C96C. The same g_00115928 table is used by the 0x10F448 snapshot variant.

name: Actor_LoadParams
summary: Copies the 0x50-byte parameter record for actor id self->f_768 from the world actor table into the instance fields at +0x30..+0x78.

name: Save_AsyncReadWorker
summary: Asynchronous save/load read worker: waits on the work event, reads length-prefixed records through Fs_ReadRecordBlock, and drives the shared work state at 0x007B0080/0x007B00E0 until the request is complete or times out.
evidence: Uses SVC 0x28 (GetSystemTick) and the 1,000,000 constant g_0011798c, calls Fs_ReadRecordBlock (0x122938), the deadline helper 0x11DF50 and the state check 0x11E374. The globals 0x007B0080/0x007B0086/0x007B00E0 are the same work object updated by Save_InitPartySnapshot's callers, and *g_00117990=5 marks completion.

name: maybe_Os_GetCurrentThreadHandle
summary: Replaces *out with a freshly queried per-thread handle, closing the previous handle with the arbitrate/close syscall first.
evidence: Calls func_001228FC(&local_10) (TLS-based query returning a handle in TLS+0x8c) and aborts via func_0011ED40 on error; if *out != 0 it issues software_interrupt(0x23) and clears it before storing the new handle. Same shape as 0x122440, which uses the 0xa0000 query instead of 0xb0000.

name: maybe_Os_ComputeDeadline
signature: void maybe_Os_ComputeDeadline(float* now, u32* base, u32* out, u32 request)
summary: Converts the current system tick and a packed timeout field into a 64-bit deadline, with the 1e6 scaling constants used by the save worker.
evidence: Reads SVC 0x28 (GetSystemTick) into the first argument, then does 64-bit multiplies by g_0011E0C4/g_0011E0CC/g_0011E0D0 and shifts by 0x12; g_0011E0C8 points at the 0x007B00B8 tick base and g_0011E0D4 is 1.0f. Only caller is Save_AsyncReadWorker 0x1170CC.

name: maybe_Save_CheckReadState
summary: Checks the save work object's stream state against the cached result codes and returns 0, a stored error, or a freshly queried status from the syscall wrapper.
evidence: Reads g_0011E438 (0x007B2D08) fields +0xc/+8 and compares them with the result constants 0xF9610C02/0xC8A10C01/0xC8A10C0D/0xC8810FEF. On the success path it clears the retry counter at +8 and on failure reports through func_0011ED40.

name: maybe_Os_GetCurrentProcessHandle
summary: Replaces *out with a queried per-process handle, releasing the old value first; companion of maybe_Os_GetCurrentThreadHandle.
evidence: Calls func_00123C9C(&local_10), which is byte-for-byte the 0xa0000 variant of func_001228FC (0xb0000). On success it stores the TLS+0x8c result into *out after software_interrupt(0x23) clears the previous value. Both are used by the save worker setup.

name: maybe_Os_GetThreadLocalValue
summary: Issues the 0xb0000 thread-local query and returns the status, storing the TLS payload word at +0x8c into *out when successful.
evidence: Reads the CP15 user-thread register, writes 0xb0000 to TLS+0x80, executes software_interrupt(0x32) and then reads TLS+0x84 (status) and +0x8c (value). func_00123C9C is the identical 0xa0000 variant; the exact nn::os wrapper name is not present in the binary.

name: Fs_ReadRecordBlock
signature: u32 Fs_ReadRecordBlock(u32 stream, u32 offset, u32* dst, int* read, int updatePosition)
summary: Reads one length-prefixed record from a stream at offset, returns the bytes read and advances the tracked stream position when requested.
evidence: Calls func_00123AD0(stream, offset, dst, max, &read) which parses the 4-byte 0xa5/14-bit-length header; it also calls func_00123A60 (stream size), func_00123A0C (seek) and func_00123AB0 (align). The state fields at +4/+8 are the current offset and retry counter, and the error path reports through func_0011ED40.

name: maybe_Os_HandleInit
summary: Creates a kernel handle through func_0012038C and stores it in *out, aborting the process through func_00118100 if creation fails.
evidence: Body: *out=0; if (*out==0 && func_0012038C(&local)>=0) { *out=local; status=0; } if (status<0) func_00118100(). Used by Save_AsyncReadWorker 0x1170CC and by 0x122484/0x122650, so it is the handle/semaphore constructor for the worker.

name: maybe_Math_AlignUp
signature: u32 maybe_Math_AlignUp(int stream, int offset, int extra)
summary: Returns offset+extra rounded up to the stream's alignment, implemented as a call to the shared align helper with the stream's alignment field at +4.
evidence: Body: func_0011CFAC(extra+offset, *(u32*)(stream+4)); return extraout_r1. 0x11CFAC is the same round-up helper used by the allocation sites (e.g. 0x14E3F4 and 0x1585F8) with a block-size argument, and the result is used as the next record offset.

name: Fs_ReadRecord
signature: u32 Fs_ReadRecord(u32 stream, u32 offset, u32 dst, u32 maxLen, u32* read)
summary: Reads a 4-byte record header (magic 0xa5 plus a 14-bit payload length) and, if the length fits in maxLen, reads the payload into dst and returns the byte count.
evidence: Header is built as local_1c[0]=0xa5 and the length is (b1 & 0x3f) | ((b1 & 0x40) ? b2<<8 : 0). func_00124B88 is the underlying read; on success *read=result and 0 is returned, otherwise the error code g_00123B64 (0xC8610C0F) is returned. Called only by Fs_ReadRecordBlock 0x122938.

name: maybe_Os_GetProcessLocalValue
summary: Issues the 0xa0000 process-local query and returns the status, storing the TLS payload word at +0x8c into *out when successful.
evidence: Identical to func_001228FC except TLS+0x80 is set to 0xa0000 instead of 0xb0000. Used by 0x122440, the process-handle companion of the thread-handle helper.

name: maybe_Os_SetThreadLocalValue
summary: Stores value in the thread-local syscall block and returns the value echoed back by the 0x007B2D2C query.
evidence: Writes g_00123D08 (0x00190040) to TLS+0x80 and value to TLS+0x84, executes software_interrupt(0x32), then returns TLS+0x84 when the status at g_00123D0C is non-negative. Called by the save state checks 0x11E374 and 0x122938's caller path.

name: maybe_Fs_ResourceFindInBucket

name: maybe_Container_DestroyObject

name: Actor_ClearLowStatusFlags

name: Ui_IsMode

name: maybe_Text_ThrowArg

name: maybe_Ui_BuildListEntries

name: maybe_Ui_PickSizeStep

name: maybe_Ui_IsMenuOpen

name: Item_PickRandomByCategory

name: Text_AdvanceTyping

name: maybe_Party_RecalcAllStats

name: maybe_Text_DecodeName

name: maybe_Party_RecalcEquipment

name: maybe_Party_ShiftSkillSlots

name: maybe_Ui_InitTransform

name: Ui_ActionPane_Init

evidence: while (func_0062F070(self)>0) func_0010EBD8(self); then func_00123594(self,self+0x34bc) and (self,self+0x34d8), func_003BDB94(self), func_002D20F4(self,1), and finally func_0029126C(self+0xbc8,1) (non-returning). name: Ui_MessagePage_UpdatePager

evidence: Calls self->f_98->f_2c (per-frame callback), decrements the repeat counter f_1164 when positive, queries self->f_10d0 vtable+0x28/+0x2c, checks input flag 0x20 in f_1bc, then calls func_006D7630(&f_120), func_00229BF4(&f_e20), func_0019B950(self) and func_00294518(&f_1c4,f_20c). The f_1bc input flags are the same ones used by the equipment list handlers.

evidence: When f_1bc bit 2 is clear it calls func_001A60A0(self+0xa08, ...), resolves the selected actor with func_0066C668/func_0064E010 and calls func_0022A144(&f_e20,...). For bit 0x102 it sets Message_SetArg(3, actor+0xca, 0) and invokes the detail vtable at f_10d0. The same f_1bc bits drive 0x199B60.

summary: Refreshes the two equipment-list panes after a selection change, recomputing the visible row and the pane scroll offsets.
evidence: Calls func_006E5628(&f_ee0,...), selects between the f_654 and f_5f4 pane objects via func_0063B5E4/func_0063B60C/func_0063B638, computes the row from f_f2c*0xc and the pane's line height, clamps it with func_006E57E4, and calls func_003E5EA4/func_001A6460 (Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim). summary: Unequips the selected equipment slot: walks the actor equipment list backwards, clears each non-cursed slot with func_001901F4 and rebuilds the equipment window.
evidence: Uses func_001DAD58(self+0x1084,self+0x1a8) and func_0062F680/func_0062F694 to read the confirmed row; resolves the actor with func_0063B5A0(self+0x1c4)/func_0035EB98, walks the equipment list backwards with func_00629150/func_006292A4, and for entries without bit 0x80 calls func_001901F4 (which shifts the 0x18-slot equipment array at +0xec and clears a slot) and func_00612008 before the named Ui_EquipmentWindow_Confirm (0x1994F4).
